turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Well, I'm here because my work is just... it's taking over everything. I do bookkeeping, and I can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. I'll stay at work for hours after everyone else leaves, even when I already checked the numbers. 

It's just, if I don't do it one more time, I get this awful feeling that something bad is going to happen and it'll be my fault. I just can't stop doing it.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes repetitive checking behaviors (going over spreadsheets again and again) performed to prevent an awful feeling that something bad will happen.

turns.doctor_question: Deep down, do you feel that this repeated checking is excessive or doesn't really make sense, or does it feel like the right and proper way to do your work?
turns.patient_response:
I know it's excessive. It really doesn't make sense to me either. I mean, like I was just saying, I'm staying at work for hours after everyone else leaves to go over the exact same spreadsheets and calculations. 

I know I already checked them, and logically I know the numbers are fine. But I just can't stop myself. If I don't go back and do it that one extra time, I get completely overwhelmed by the feeling that something bad is going to happen and it'll be my fault. So, yeah, deep down I know it's way too much and not the normal way to work, but I just have to keep doing it.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive checking of spreadsheets that they recognize as excessive and illogical, which they feel compelled to do to prevent a feared outcome.
